newsitem.title: USA: US group seeks FTC bar of Texaco/Shell merger.
newsitem.headline: US group seeks FTC bar of Texaco/Shell merger.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission should slam the brakes on the merger plan between Texaco Inc and Shell Oil Co, a consumer group said Tuesday, alleging it was anti-competitive and anti-consumer.
"This merger will sharply reduce competition in major gasoline markets," said Edwin Rothschild of Citizen Action, a Washington D.C.-based watchdog group.
"If allowed, (the merger) would set a dangerous precedent,"
Rothschild said in a statement. "Such a combination is aimed at destroying rather than enhancing competition among refiners and gasoline retailers."

The transaction would merge downstream operations of Texaco, Shell, and Star Enterprise, a joint venture between Texaco and Saudi Aramco, the state oil company of Saudi Arabia. The merged entity would control 15 percent of the U.S. petroleum products market, with assets worth $10 billion.
Rothschild contended the merger would hurt consumers in urban areas by creating "regional giants," firms less inclined to engage in competition in areas where there are only a few major players.
"Southern California, where competition in the gasoline market is already severely limited, will become a nightmare for motorists," he said.
"The proposed consolidation may be good for 'Big Oil,' but it spells disaster for free market competition," he added.
The group's concerns echo those of U.S. oilworker unions, who fear job cuts would be in store as the firms consolidate and smaller players get potentially squeezed out of the market.
So far, the companies have not publicly addressed the merger's specifics, saying only that they will spend the next few months attempting to close the deal.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
